inputs.text: It's been five months since that ceasefire was announced in Gaza, but airstrikes are still slaughtering civilians and the humanitarian crisis for Palestinians is as desperate as ever. This isn't just some temporary fallout—it's a deliberate stripping away of any connection these communities have to their pre-war lives, forcing them into an even darker, more brutal existence under constant assault. The powerful forces involved are showing once again how structural inequality and historical oppression keep vulnerable populations trapped in cycles of violence and dispossession. As 56-year-old Ahmed Baroud, a father of five currently displaced in Deir al-Balah, described it: “Drones never stop buzzing overhead, gunfire and shelling continue almost daily and naval boats fire towards fishermen.” This demands real institutional reform to protect the oppressed and end these injustices.
